subject: livestock being stolen, and guarding a herd against it
citation: Farmers' perceptions of stock theft in South Africa (PLOS ONE, 2024)
Welfare impact of stock theft, Nyandeni (SciELO SA, 2025)

farm_products: Growing of crops combined with farming of animals(mixed farming)

claims.text: Livestock is a high-value, movable target that is easy to convert into cash or cultural goods, so theft becomes a rational choice whenever guardianship is absent.
When herding labour is unaffordable and grazing camps are distant, livestock left unguarded become an open invitation to theft.
objections: How will this policy help me afford a herder when I am already struggling to get by?

claims.text: Lenient sentences signal that the state does not take livestock theft seriously, so only the threat of lifetime imprisonment is seen as a real deterrent.
objections: How will this policy make the punishment harsh enough that thieves actually fear it?

claims.text: Cultural ceremonies create a steady, unregulated demand for livestock that does not require proof of ownership, so theft surges around traditional events.
objections: How will this policy make it harder to sell stolen livestock at traditional events without a certificate of ownership?

claims.text: Without widespread branding or tattooing, stolen livestock become anonymous goods, making detection and recovery nearly impossible.
objections: How will this policy help me identify my animals when they are taken far away in the dark?

confidence: Mixed-methods and review-based, two-study synthesis covering Eastern Cape communal areas — mechanisms are well-attested in participant perception, but magnitudes and causal weights are not quantified.
